Title: Maternal, newborn and child deaths and illness are reduced among displaced and host communities in six localities of Kassala, Gedaref, Blue Nile, White Nile, Sennar and Red Sea States, Sudan

Women, newborns and children under five in the six localities use quality, timely maternal, newborn and child health, immunisation and nutrition-screening services at supported primary health care centres and through mobile teams
Midwives, nurses and community health workers are competent in emergency obstetric and newborn care, IMNCI and immunisation
Emergency obstetric and newborn care (EmONC) training for midwives and nurses (two batches)
IMNCI, immunisation and nutrition-screening refresher for primary health care staff
Monthly on-the-job mentoring and supportive supervision at supported facilities
Supported primary health care centres provide safe delivery, newborn care and referral (rehabilitated delivery rooms, referral transport)
Rehabilitate and equip delivery rooms and newborn corners at 12 primary health care centres (two per locality)
Operate the community referral transport scheme (ambulances and motorcycle-ambulances)
Essential MNCH medicines, vaccines and nutrition supplies are continuously available at supported facilities with a working cold chain
Monthly MNCH supply forecasting, ordering and last-mile delivery
Monthly stock and cold-chain checks at supported facilities
Displaced and remote communities are reached by monthly mobile integrated outreach (ANC, PNC, immunisation, malnutrition screening)
Monthly mobile integrated outreach in displacement gathering sites and remote villages
Catch-up vaccination rounds for zero-dose and under-vaccinated children
Caregivers and communities in the six localities practise safe motherhood, early care-seeking and optimal infant and young child feeding
Community health volunteers identify pregnancies, sick children and malnutrition early and refer
Train community health volunteers on pregnancy identification, danger signs and referral
Village pregnancy and under-five registration with referral cards
Caregivers, men and community leaders support facility delivery, immunisation and infant and young child feeding practices
Mother support groups and community education sessions (feeding, danger signs, immunisation)
Radio messages and community dialogues on maternal and child danger signs
State ministries of health use MNCH data to manage services
Monthly state MNCH data review and action meetings
Baseline and endline MNCH coverage survey
